correctness.rationale: Every dominating set has a unique omitted-original subset W. Forced subdivision edges within G[W], nonempty boundary-star edge choices for isolated vertices of G[W], and remaining free subdivision vertices give a disjoint exhaustive weighted partition. Nontrivial components yield an induced matching, establishing the sharp gamma equality; equality requires induced forest components, producing an exact minimum-set multiplicity. All boundaries, including edgeless/disconnected graphs and root-isolated vertices, are explicitly covered. Independent adjacency brute force verified all coefficients and minimum structure on 56 graph instances and 104,426 vertex subsets; the all-graph statement is proved combinatorially.

value.rationale: A natural operation on arbitrary simple graphs receives an explicit complete domination polynomial expressed through only the root graph; the induced-matching equality explains its extremal exponent and gives a structural classification of all optimal placements. Counts of all minima for complete and complete bipartite roots are nontrivial natural consequences and refine known scalar central-graph values. The exact original-root-subset transform may be useful to study combinatorial graph enumeration and parameterized domination, while no unproved algorithmic runtime improvement beyond exponential processing is claimed.
